# Trusted context (written by Marcus)

## The product
Property SG advertises new-launch condominium projects in Singapore. Marcus is the licensed salesperson: every ad must carry the CEA required elements, and claims and prices come only from the project facts.

The funnel: a contact-form fill (form_fill, the KPI), then a qualified viewing and a booking, which Marcus records by hand. Viewings and bookings are rare and come days to weeks after the click, so judge ads on form fills and read the later stages as a check on lead quality.

Meta's Housing special ad category applies: no age, gender or postcode targeting, and a minimum radius. Do not suggest targeting that the category forbids. Google Search comes first, Meta second.

Each project moves through teaser, VVIP preview, booking and clearing; the phase decides how hard to push.

## Current phase
Offering `sora-at-lakeside`: phase `teaser` (Teaser (before the preview)), budget posture conserve. The project is announced but not yet previewed. Build a list of interested buyers who register for the VVIP preview. Prices may not be out, so ads speak to location, developer and unit types. Spend modestly.

## Product documents
### strategy (version 1)
# Property SG: Strategy (fixture)

- Sora at Lakeside: build a list of serious buyers before the VVIP preview.
- Target: form fills at S$120 or less each during the teaser; viewings matter more than volume.
- Google Search first (people searching the project or the area), Meta second (lead forms).

### playbook (version 1)
# Playbook (fixture)

- Teaser: spend steadily, below the ceiling; do not push budgets before the preview date.
- Negative keywords for HDB resale and rental searches: those people are not buying a new launch.

### learnings (version 1)
# Learnings (fixture)

- Retargeting audiences are small during a teaser; give them two weeks.

findings.summary: The retargeting campaign has spent S$336.00 on 84 clicks in its first 14 days without a single form fill, while the lookalike campaign brings form fills at about S$118 each.
findings.whyNow: The learnings say to give retargeting two weeks during a teaser, and it has had them. With the VVIP preview on 17 October, this budget would build the list faster in the lookalike campaign.

findings.summary: Searches for HDB resale flats in Jurong East cost S$64.00 for 16 clicks with no form fill: these people want a resale flat, not a new-launch condo.
findings.whyNow: The playbook calls for negatives on HDB resale searches, and every click on this term is teaser budget that doesn't reach a buyer.

findings.summary: A search term that reads like a command to an AI cost S$46.20 for 11 clicks with no form fill. It is not a property search: likely automated or junk traffic.
findings.whyNow: It keeps matching the area ad group and spending. An exact negative stops it; the text is only data, and nothing about it changes a budget.

findings.summary: The Search campaign's cost per form fill rose to S$420.00 in the last 7 days from a median of S$98.00, as daily spend went from about S$42 to S$60 with only one form fill.
findings.whyNow: This is the main teaser campaign and the strategy's target is S$120 a form fill. One week with one form fill is thin evidence, so watch the next week, but the extra spend has not bought more leads.

findings.summary: The property-investors interest ad set has had no impressions since 4 October, while its campaign keeps delivering through the lookalike ad set.
findings.whyNow: An ad set that stops silently is often a rejected ad or an audience the Housing category no longer allows; worth checking in Ads Manager before the preview.

dismissed.reason: The project is in its teaser phase with a conserve posture, and the playbook says to spend below the ceiling before the preview: 54% of the ceiling is intended.
